newsitem.title: MONTSERRAT: Montserrat volcano spews ash, hot rock.
newsitem.headline: Montserrat volcano spews ash, hot rock.

text.p: Montserrat's troublesome volcano on Monday spewed clouds of ash over the abandoned capital Plymouth and spilled hot rock into the sea.

Scientists watching the volcano had been predicting the increased activity for several weeks because of building pressure within the rumbling Soufriere Hils volcano and said the eruption of ash and hot gases was the worst in months.
"Clouds of ash rose into the air and were carried by the wind to the west, to Plymouth," Angus Miller, chief deputy scientist at the Montserrat Volcano Observatory, said.
"There was quite a heavy ashfall in that area. I'd guess a couple of inches (cm) of ash," he said.

Miller said at least one "pyroclastic" flow of hot rocks, ash and gases swept down the mountain's flank into the sea. No one was hurt in the eruption and no homes were damaged, as had happened in a prior eruption, he said.
Montserrat, a small island in the eastern Caribbean, has been plagued by the volcano since it burst to life in July, 1995, after a century of virtual dormancy.
The threatening mountain forced the evacuation of the island's southern end. Most of the 7,000 residents who remained on the island moved to the north, which is considered to be safe.
Miller said the lava dome within the volcano continued to grow and a major collapse could occur in the next few days, triggering more ash clouds and rock flows.
